newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone peace talks postponed until July 29.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone peace talks postponed until July 29.

text.p: A second round of peace talks between Sierra Leone's military rulers and their West African neighbours in Ivory Coast has been put back by four days until July 29, state radio reported on Wednesday.

Diplomats in Conakry, capital of neighbouring Guinea, told Reuters by telephone that West African foreign ministers who wwould take part in the talks had put back the meeting to allow the junta more time to meet their demand.
"The demand by the junta in Sierra Leone about the return of constitutional rule in that country without (ousted president Ahmad Tejan) Kabbah is a non-starter," one said.
Diplomatic and U.N. sources said that the foreign ministers of Nigeria, Guinea, Ghana and Ivory Coast had talks with Kabbah in Conakry on Tuesday.
Soldiers toppled Kabbah on May 25. Rebels, who took up arms in 1991 but agreed on peace last November, rallied to the coup.
West African foreign ministers decided in Guinea on June 26 to use dialogue and economic sanctions to persuade the junta to reinstate Kabbah, but they retained a military option.

A statement after July 18 talks in the Ivorian commercial capital Abidjan said the two sides agreed to "resolve all issues related to the Sierra Leone crisis peacefully" and would "work towards early restoration of constitutional order".

They agreed an immediate nationwide truce but the local commander of Nigerian troops in Freetown under a pre-coup defence pact has hinted at military action if Kabbah was not reinstated, warning civilians to avoid military targets.
